title: The right adjoint for a finite etale morphism
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and $n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X,V$ be schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible, and let $e:V\to X$ be a finite etale morphism [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism, def-weil-etale-morphism]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], the module direct image $e_*$ [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] is exact. Its total derived functor [def-weil-derived-direct-image] is computed termwise, and there is an adjunction on the entire, possibly unbounded, derived categories:
$$
Re_*=e_*:D(V_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\rightleftarrows D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A):e^*,\qquad e_*\dashv e^*.
$$
Here $e^*$ is the exact inverse image, applied termwise [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. For the compact-support assertion, additionally use the ambient setting of the source unit: $X,V$ are finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$ has characteristic $p\ne\ell$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], and $e$ is a $k$-morphism. For compact-support direct image [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], use the proper compactification $c=(\operatorname{id}_V,e)$. With this choice on the entire derived category,
$$
Re_!^{c}=Re_*=e_*\dashv e^*.
$$
On the subcategory where compactification independence has been established, this is the usual identification $Re_!=Re_*$.

proof.text: An etale map is flat and unramified [def-weil-etale-morphism, def-weil-unramified-morphism], so its diagonal is an open immersion. An open immersion induces isomorphisms on local rings [def-weil-open-immersion], hence is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism]. Thus an etale map is flat with flat diagonal, i.e. weakly etale [def-weil-weakly-etale-morphism]. In particular $e$ is an object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$. By [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization], its slice site is $V_{\mathrm{proet}}$ and the restricted constant ring is $A_V$. The inverse image $e^*$ is restriction to this slice: the direct-image formula [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] on a test object $W$ is $F(W\times_XV)$, the direct image for the localization morphism, and the inverse images of this morphism agree. Apply [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] with $\mathcal O=A_X$ and slice object $V$. Denote its exact left adjoint to $e^*$ by $J_e$ to distinguish slice extension by zero from the compact-support derived functor. Thus $J_e\dashv e^*$ and both $J_e,e^*$ are exact. For each point $x\in X$, [lem-weil-pbc-finite-etale-etale-local-split] gives an etale neighbourhood $U\to X$ on which $V_U=\coprod_{s\in S_U}U$, with $S_U$ finite. These neighbourhoods are jointly surjective. Their maps are flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-weil-etale-morphism], and hence open by [lem-weil-pbc-flat-lfp-open]. Over each affine test open, cover their inverse images by affine opens; their images are open and cover the test open, so quasi-compactness selects finitely many. Together with weak etaleness this is precisely the covering criterion of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]; the sheet count is allowed to vary with $U$.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: local splitting and the slice-site interpretation

proof.text: Fix one splitting neighbourhood $U$ and write $S=S_U$. A test object $W\to V_U$ is covered by its disjoint inverse images $W_s$ of the sheets. The sheaf condition says $F(W)=\prod_s F(W_s)$, with zero value on an empty intersection. Thus a sheaf on $V_U$ is exactly a family $(F_s)_{s\in S}$ of module sheaves on $U$, and module maps are exactly families of module maps [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. The direct-image formula [def-weil-proetale-module-direct-image] becomes $e_*F|_U=\prod_sF_s$ by applying that sheaf condition to $W\times_UV_U=\coprod_sW$. Restriction inverse image is the diagonal $N\mapsto(N)_s$ [lem-weil-proetale-weakly-etale-localization]. The presheaf formula [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] and its sheafification in [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact] give $J_eF|_U=\bigoplus_sF_s$: a map $W\to V_U$ is locally the inclusion of one sheet, so its generator is locally the corresponding summand generator, and restricting these generators gives exactly the restriction maps of that sum. Restriction to a slice uses the same covering families [def-pur-localized-ringed-site], so sheafification and this local description agree. For finitely many module sheaves this sum is also the sectionwise product: the coordinatewise module operations and restrictions satisfy the sheaf axiom, and the sum of finitely many coordinate maps has the coproduct universal property.

source.place: Proof, first paragraph: finite tuple formulas, with sheaf condition and extension-by-zero construction expanded

proof.text: On this neighbourhood the canonical map $b:\bigoplus_sF_s\to\prod_tF_t$ has $(t,s)$-component $\operatorname{id}$ for $t=s$ and $0$ otherwise. Its inverse is $\sum_s\iota_s\pi_s$; composing in either order gives the identity by the finite coordinate calculation. For a change of splitting, refine the overlap into the open-and-closed inverse images of the sheets under the two splittings; on each such piece the change is a permutation. Relabelling $s,t$ preserves both the equality test $s=t$ in $b$ and the sum defining its inverse. Hence both local maps agree on overlaps. Apply [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] to $J_eF$ and $e_*F$ over $X$, and to the reversed pair, to glue $b$ and its inverse. The composites and naturality squares agree after the covering and therefore globally by uniqueness in that same lemma. This gives a natural isomorphism $J_e\cong e_*$. Consequently $e_*$ is exact and $e_*\dashv e^*$, by the exact adjunction of step 1. The empty sheet set gives the zero sheaf on both sides and the unique isomorphism; no nonempty-fibre assumption is used.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: permutation compatibility and gluing, with inverse maps and exactness

proof.text: Here are the unit, counit and triangles of the resulting adjunction, to fix its direction. On a splitting neighbourhood the unit at $F=(F_s)_s$ has $s$-component the inclusion $F_s\to\bigoplus_tF_t$; the counit at $N$ is $\bigoplus_sN\to N$, $(n_s)_s\mapsto\sum_sn_s$. These maps commute with restrictions and permutations, so their uniqueness under [lem-pur-sheaf-hom-cover-gluing] agrees with the adjunction obtained in step 3. The first triangle on a vector $\iota_s(m)$ sends it into the $s$-summand of $\bigoplus_s\bigoplus_tF_t$ and then sums the outer coordinate, returning $\iota_s(m)$. The second triangle on the $s$-component $N$ is $N\xrightarrow{\iota_s}\bigoplus_tN\xrightarrow{\sum}N$, the identity. Equality of sheaf maps is checked on the covering by uniqueness of gluing. For $S=\varnothing$ the first identity is the identity of zero and the second is an identity in the zero product category.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: explicit adjunction maps and the two triangle calculations

proof.text: Apply [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated] to the two exact additive functors $e_*$ and $e^*$. Their termwise functors preserve quasi-isomorphisms: exactness identifies cohomology in each integer degree with the functor applied to cohomology. The unit and counit of step 4 give degreewise chain maps, since their naturality commutes with each differential, and their two composite chain maps are the identities degreewise. Localization at quasi-isomorphisms therefore carries these natural transformations and identities to the unbounded derived categories and defines the adjunction there. If $K\to I$ is the K-injective resolution used in [def-weil-derived-direct-image], then $e_*K\to e_*I$ is a quasi-isomorphism by exactness. Thus termwise $e_*$ computes $Re_*$, and [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] already identifies $e^*$ with termwise inverse image. No boundedness or constructibility is needed in this passage.

source.place: Proof, second paragraph: passage to complexes and ordinary unbounded derived categories

proof.text: The map $e$ is proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper]. In the finite-type setting of the compact-support clause, $c=(\operatorname{id}_V,e)$ is therefore a compactification. By the formula in [def-weil-compact-support-candidate], $Re_!^c=Re_*\,(\operatorname{id}_V)_!$ on the entire derived category. Extension by zero for the identity is the identity: in [def-weil-extension-by-zero-presheaf] every test object has its unique structure map to the final object $V$, so the extension presheaf has one summand equal to the original sheaf and needs no further sheafification. Hence $Re_!^c=Re_*$ on the entire derived category, and step 5 proves the displayed adjunction. On the etale-origin subcategory specified in [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed], the chosen compactification superscript may be suppressed. This step invokes no unbounded compactification-independence assertion.
